result.title: CineRecon: Benchmarking Frontier Models for Agentic Cinematic Reconstruction
result.summary: Reconstructing reference videos as editable dynamic 3D scenes is an important path toward controllable video generation for filmmaking: these scenes provide modifiable, renderable visual proxies that enable explicit control over scene layout, subject actions, and camera behavior. To evaluate agents' ability to reconstruct editable dynamic 3D scenes from dynamic reference videos, we introduce CineRecon, a benchmark comprising 50 reference videos and 360 annotated evaluation clips. The reference videos span film, real-world footage, and games. Given a complete video, an agent uses tools to construct, animate, render, and refine its reconstruction. We evaluate this task under three representation settings: Proxy, Simplified, and Detailed. These settings increase geometric and appearance requirements while retaining the same requirements for spatial relations, camera behavior, and subject dynamics. This design tests whether agents can reproduce the events in a video when detailed appearance is unnecessary, and how performance changes as representation requirements increase. For evaluation, we construct checklists that associate observable properties and events with specific entities and times. A vision-language judge compares timestamp-aligned reference and rendered frames across 11 categories, grouped into camera, static, and dynamic consistency dimensions. We evaluate 12 models using their corresponding agent harnesses and find failures across all three dimensions. Subject motions and interactions remain difficult to reproduce even under the Proxy setting.

AI.brief_summary: 提出 CineRecon 基准：用 50 段参考视频与 360 个标注片段，考察智能体在 Proxy、Simplified、Detailed 三种表示要求下重建可编辑动态 3D 场景的能力，并以 VLM 评判器对时间戳对齐的渲染帧打分。
AI.relevance_reason: 其表示层级受控比较与按时间戳对齐的清单式 VLM 评判，可能为 LVR 中「任务必要视觉信息是否保留」「证据使用是否到位」的评测设计提供线索，可供核查；但论文本体属视频与 3D 重建，与 latent 推理状态联系较远。
